title: Shibboleth (Judges 12:1–6)
hookLine: a word said differently becomes a death sentence

cards: A ford on the Jordan, where the river runs shallow enough to wade. Men of Gilead are guarding it. A traveler comes down to the water and asks to cross.
Are you an Ephraimite? He says no. So they ask him to say one word.
"Say now Shibboleth: and he said Sibboleth: for he could not frame to pronounce it right." That's all it takes. One sound, a little off, and they seize him at the water's edge.

teach.b: It starts with hurt pride. The men of Ephraim cross over to Jephthah after his victory, furious. Why didn't you call us to fight with you?
We'll burn your house down over you. Ephraim made almost the same complaint once before, to Gideon, a few chapters back.
Gideon answered softly: what have I done, compared with you? And their anger cooled. Jephthah answers with his own grievance, and then with war.
Insults fly. The Gileadites win, and seize the fords so the Ephraimites can't get home. And at the river, the test isn't what you believe, or what you've done.
It's how your mouth makes one sound. The word itself is ordinary.

teach.h: AN EAR OF GRAIN, A FLOOD.
teach.b: Elsewhere in the Bible, shibboleth is an ear of grain, in Pharaoh's dream of full and thin ears, and in a psalm it's a flood of water rising. Nothing holy about it.
Just a word with a sh at the front that some people said as s. And these aren't foreigners at the ford. Gilead and Ephraim are kin, tribes of one people, descended in the story from the same family.
That's the grief of it: brothers divided by an accent, and a word for grain turned into a test of who's in and who's out.

how: Jews read the shibboleth story in Judges 12 as part of the Former Prophets, often alongside Gideon's soft answer to the same tribe in Judges 8 as a study in how a quarrel between kin grows or cools.

o: a secret password known only to the soldiers
an ordinary word for grain, turned into a test
a holy word spoken only by the priests of Gilead

games.q: one word divides — tap the pairs.
p: guarded the fords of the Jordan

s: the Ephraimites failed because they didn't know the password
they knew the word; they said it differently: sibboleth.
Ephraim had made the same complaint to Gideon, and he calmed them
Gideon answered softly, and their anger cooled (Judges 8:1–3).
it's an ordinary word, used elsewhere in the Bible for an ear of grain and for a flood of water.

games.q: you're Jephthah, just home from war. the men of Ephraim storm in: why didn't you call us? we'll burn your house down. what do you do?
o: answer with your own grievance, then fight.
say nothing and let them go.
games.why: Jephthah says he did call and they didn't come, then gathers Gilead and fights. Gideon, facing the same anger, had answered softly.

practice: Bring to mind a voice that sounds different from yours, an accent, a dialect, one word said another way, and notice whether the mind starts sorting: one of us, not one of us.
Then picture the person behind the voice at their own kitchen table, saying that word the way their mother did.

wordCard.voice: Shibboleth. An ordinary Hebrew word, an ear of grain, that became a test at a river crossing because some people said it differently.

orig.note: Hebrew: an ear of grain, or a flowing stream; the test word at the fords of the Jordan.

carryVoice: Your line: one word divides. Gideon's soft answer was the other way. Day seven hundred twenty-two.
